steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Colonel.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: We meet again, Skamandros.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You don't seem one bit surprised.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Surprised?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: No, from the first I met you, I have not been one bit surprised—you were bound to mingle with this rabble, simply because of that cheap sympathy you learned from your noble etiquette classes.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You shadowed us?!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: I'd rather term this rational management.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Regardless of anything, I must thank you. If it weren't for your leading the way, I wouldn't have such a sublime opportunity to net all these rot-eating vermin in one fell swoop.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: You hide fairly deep most of the time, don't you?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: I confess I'm quite curious. What made you so audacious as to gather up? Could it be that from the outcomes of your last few pathetic, negligible sneak attacks, you mistakenly believed County Hillock was already under your control?

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: A-Ahem... Colonel, sir, I believe there may be some misunderstanding at play here.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: That is wrong, Baron Bolton. There is no misunderstanding between us whatsoever. I am pristinely clear about your confidential lowly dealings.

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: It's only some of my good friends and family gathered here today. That, I can guarantee you on my very name—

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Shut up kindly, good sir. The honor you've inherited from your ancestry purchases nothing in my eyes.

steps.name: Pretentious Noblewoman
steps.text: Y—You have some nerve saying that!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: The one dishonoring your so-called noble reputation isn't me by far. Who are they, reveling in the position and wealth Victoria accords them, then turning to secretly collude with the most lowly rebels of them all?

steps.name: Pretentious Noblewoman
steps.text: This is out-and-out slander!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: I'm starting to be sick of this blather now. You rabble should behave as the rabble outside, weeping in the light of a blaze while you confess your own wrongdoings.
Just as he said, from outside the window come wails and cries, the glass reflecting speckled points of fire.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: (Leader, look outside! It's not just in here, he's got the Tarans from the whole block surrounded too.)

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: (He's not exaggeratin' at all. He's cowerin' ordinary residents with military force.)

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: (I've been around that street before—a huge portion of them are elderly and children!)

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: (With methods suddenly this radical, it seems there's some other information he has a hold on. He's very likely to have hidden intel about the spectre force from us.)

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: (Nothin' from Triangle?)

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: (No comms at all since afternoon.)

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: (Flip. Could somethin' have happened to them?)

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: (There's no point in worrying. What's more pressing right now is we should hold the troops back as much as we can.)

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: (We can't stay trapped in here, at least...)

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: You, the Vouivre over there. You are not to think of breaking out through the wall. Before my questioning bears fruit, no one is allowed to leave this room.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Ugh, he spotted me!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Come out! I see you! No movement, I want you to kneel here and behave!

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: Agh!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Is there anyone else in your home? Speak up!

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: N—No...

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: You're not hiding anyone? I'll see for myself. Listen, so long as I see you move a muscle, no matter what you're trying at, I will immediately shoot your head through.

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: *Whimper*...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: What are you doing?!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Who are you, coming from nowhere and running in front of my crossbow? Watch your own head!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Wait, hold on, I recognize you. You're that guard of honor from Adams's group, aren't you? I saw you at the New Year do. Your group didn't get any order to move. What are you doing here?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I have another assignment nearby I'm on.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Fine, then, each to their own. Don't you start getting in my way.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: (That lass called Bagpipe told me I could step forth too, change the situation.)

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: (Can I, though...? I have to try, at least...)

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Did they... do something wrong, to be treated this rough?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: You're asking me? Why don't you go ask them?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: What are you crying for? Wasn't it you lot, harboring thugs, giving them food and drink, feeding them information?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Do you have evidence?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Evidence? You want evidence? Do the wounds on the 9th and 13th count? Each one of their bodies still warm?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Some died by eerie Originium Arts, some died by makes of crossbows and sabers identical to the ones we carry, and some had traces on their necks left behind by farming tools.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Our heads cut off with threshers like wheat, bodies crushed thin and flat by tractors like plowed land—have you ever... pictured that? The devastation?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Ulp...

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: That's right, you should want to puke. I saw with my own eyes, and I recognized who that head used to belong to, and for an entire afternoon, I puked. I couldn't stop.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: They... why would they treat their own like this... this is too cruel!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Hah, damn right you are. Behaving never suited them.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Now you understand this serves them right, don't you?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: What are you still blanking out for?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: So... these are all bad people? Just because... they're all Tarans?

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: *Sob*... agh... I haven't done a thing, Sir...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: She's crying.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Her husband already passed away from Oripathy, and her child's only pushing ten... is someone bereft like this really going to be a murderer?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: How have I not gotten it through to you?! They're all one kind, do you understand? Even if this woman and her child haven't done anything yet, they're all together in this.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: If it wasn't a Taran, in front of you all, but some other Victorian citizen...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Would you still insist on treating them all as thugs?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: If... I'm just saying, if, from the very beginning, there were never those discriminatory laws, if Tarans could've earned as much as anyone else, gotten the same chance at healthcare...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Wouldn't none of this conflict have ever happened?!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Alright, guard of honor, if you love asking questions so much, keep asking. There won't be an answer. Nobody's got any way of answering you. I'm essentially done searching this house by now anyway, so it's onto the next one.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Hey! I said I was going, not that you could stand up!

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: *Sob*... Ah... don't take me, Craig can't be without me...

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Shut it with all the sobbing! Wailing about your child all day long just so I can go soft on you, is it?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Just let her go.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Eugh, you. Fine, I'm busy anyway. I can afford to ignore this woman.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: But just to warn you, you might be protecting them now with all your kind heart, but be careful they don't blow you sky-high without blinking the moment your head is turned.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Don't you forget, after all, you and them aren't the same kind. Have you seen the looks in their eyes before? In their eyes, no matter how you behave, you'll always be one of us.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Just go... Please.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: *spits* Don't say I didn't warn you.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Phew... you've not been harmed, no?

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: It's lucky. After me and Saoirse talked, I couldn't shake this nervous feeling, and I had to come back and take a look.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: So it really can be a bit of use... to stand up.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Come on, I'll help you back inside. For tonight... no, tomorrow as well, don't go out, please. There's ruffians outside, as well as... um, at any rate, Hillock won't be as safe for these next few days.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Right, and where's your boy...? Craig? He's not at home?

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: Craig... he... *gulp*...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: He's been taken away by the soldiers, hasn't he?!

steps.name: Sorrowful Woman
steps.text: I... I don't know...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I need to go and find him.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Hill!

steps.name: Adjutant Hill
steps.text: Colonel, we've just apprehended this one in this corridor outside, right as he was attempting to dive out of the window.

steps.name: Frightened Youth
steps.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry...

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Let me guess, this boy is some follower of yours, preparing to send word to somebody or other?

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: I... (Wipes off a cold sweat)

steps.name: Greedy Businessman
steps.text: I want a lawyer! I know the Mayor and quite a few Members too... Let me go, you have no authority to keep us held like this!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: It seems my guess was dead on. Every one of you has some involvement.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: You may speak. All I need to know is where your co-conspirators are hiding.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: How about this, then. I'll count to three—

steps.name: Frightened Youth
steps.text: Aaaargh! Don't, don't kill me!

steps.name: Pretentious Noblewoman
steps.text: My goodness... Why must you have me see such cruelty?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: You can't be doin' this!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Really? Skamandros, tell your subordinate, do I have the right to be doing this?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Leader...!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Provisional administrative law... In the event we are unable to receive direct orders from Londinium, Colonel Hamilton is the highest acting commander of the County Hillock barracks, and does possess the authority to impose martial law on the whole city.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I know! But if he's seriously goin' to do this, then he's essentially declarin' a formal war on the hidden army!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I fear that one thing they've said is right. We are already situated within in a war.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: But we barely know more than nothin' about that army.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: We're stark open and they're still in the shadows. No matter what, I don't feel now was good timin' to open fire first.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Timing! They never picked any timing when they launched attacks on us unilaterally.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Colonel, even if you won't take any suggestion from our team, I still must express clear opposition to the course of action you are about to adopt.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Very thankful for your one scrap of self-awareness shown.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: In honesty, I'm not fond of doing this either. As long as they'd left me another choice, I would never be willing to break the Empire's laws.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Yet we're out of time. The hidden enemy is closing in with each step.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Isn't this as you said too, Skamandros? You, too, came to drag the ghosts out into the sunlight!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: If we don't seize this opportunity, and force all the remaining conspirators out, then we will have lost County Hillock before the morrow.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Colonel, I believe the more critical the juncture, the more each step we choose will lead to divergent results.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I'm sure, there are many innocents among those present. You can take them away first, and then...

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: No, I have no time to squander on pointless interrogation. Right now, on this very spot, these rabblesome dregs will make clear where in the world their members are hidden!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Hill, do it! We've tarried for long enough—

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: ...Colonel.

steps.name: Hamilton
steps.text: And who in Hell's bloody bells are you?

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: Please arrest me. I am Baron Bolton's guest, and will know much more than any of these poor young people, rendered near-unconscious.

steps.name: Wildly Ambitious Baron
steps.text: Seamus! What are you doing stepping up?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Seamus... Seamus Williams. You're that bard?

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: I am, Colonel.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Very good. I'd been meaning to look for you, so as to keep you from continuing to incite those imbeciles with your blither.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Williams...

steps.name: Bard Williams
steps.text: You need not fear, ma'am. I ought to thank the Colonel, for just a moment ago, I worked out how my poem should conclude.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Seize him!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: A... ball? Where have I seen this...

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Hill! Order those posted outside to find the rabble who broke that window...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: No, this isn't right.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: There's a sound... comin' from the ball!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Get down!!!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Who—Who was that? Where did you show up from?!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Argh—! It's—It's you lot! G—Go inform the Colonel double-time, 4th has run into the thugs, in an alley by the square—

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: This group has been annihilated.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Leader, the nearby Taran blocks have all been occupied by ours.

steps.name: Wounded Youth
steps.text: You lot are...

steps.name: Wounded Youth
steps.text: It—It's you?! You're the... the one we've been waiting for!

steps.name: Wounded Youth
steps.text: You actually gave your hand to me... I...

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: There'll be no one else to oppress you again.

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: And you'll never need anyone's arm to lean on again.

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: From this moment on, you can walk freely upon this soil, by your own power.

steps.name: Wounded Youth
steps.text: Thank you... oh, thank you! Everything I did, it really was right!

steps.name: Wounded Youth
steps.text: There'll be a day for us Tarans... when we can have our own city, we can walk heads held high in the streets, we'll never be given injust treatment again!

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: Yes. It is precisely for that day that we come.

steps.name: Wounded Youth
steps.text: Leader, you have to see! It's—It's the fire we lit in your service!

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: The ballroom...

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: According to the report Madam Mandragora gave, the barracks' top brass are all in there.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: However, an explosion of that scale would only give the barracks' arrogance pause. Unfortunately, it could never wipe them out.

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: Apart from the barracks, who else is there?

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Some locals who will us well. They learned of some of our inside matters, and the heads' thoughts are, for the overall picture, we can't leave anyone alive to tell tales.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: They also said, if you won't make a move, they will themselves.

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: ...In the end... my fire is quicker.

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: Tell them, I know what should be done—

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: I'll take the ballroom.

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Yes, Leader—your fire will break these shackles that have chained us for centuries!
